title: POC scoping - Quality Eval Plan (CareEdge Health)
redwood_attendees: Liam O'Connor (Customer Success, briefly on call)
summary: POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan: define golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring approach, workload sizing, benchmarks and timelines. Agreement to share eval dataset and run Redwood-hosted benchmarks; security questions (PHI, KMS, VPC) to be clarified before pilot.
next_steps: Send proposed eval dataset + golden prompts by 2026-08-07
Share security pack (SOC2, architecture diagram, Private deployment checklist) by 2026-08-06
Schedule benchmarking run (SE + customer) week of 2026-08-10
Follow-up meeting to review pilot results on 2026-08-20
action_items: Evan Chambers: send proposed eval dataset and golden prompts by 2026-08-07
Sofia Patel: prepare benchmark config (throughput/latency + quality tests) and runbook by 2026-08-09
Dr. Maya Singh: provide PHI-sanitized sample dataset, target labels and success criteria by 2026-08-09
Priya Nair: confirm data residency / KMS and whether Private deployment required for pilot by 2026-08-07
transcript:
00:00 Evan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm evan from redwood inference, this is sofia our solutions engineer. quick roll call?
00:08 Dr. Maya: maya here, thanks. carlos and priya and sanjay on our side.
00:14 Evan (Redwood): awesome. agenda today — we want to agree the quality eval plan for the poc: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring approach, and then map to workload sizing and benchmarks and timeline. sound good?
00:25 Carlos (CareEdge): yea that's great. our key metric is extraction accuracy on clinical notes and hallucination tolerance — we must not invent meds or dosages.
00:35 Sofia (Redwood SE): important, we'll call that "hallucination tolerance" and set a hard threshold. for extraction tasks we usually measure token-level F1 and span EM for exact match on structured fields. is that aligned?
00:47 Dr. Maya: yes, span EM for critical fields (medication, dosage, diagnosis) and F1 for entities is good. also format checks — output must follow our JSON schema, otherwise it's a fail.
00:59 Priya (CareEdge): and from security perspective: can you run this on dedicated capacity or private? PHI is involved. we need KMS, audit logs, and SOC2 attestation.
01:12 Evan (Redwood): we can do this three ways: hosted with strict retention and encryption, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). for pilot we often start in dedicated to hit throughput and cost targets but if policy requires private we can shift. we'll send the security pack with SOC2, encryption, SSO/SAML info.
01:27 Sanjay (CareEdge): timeline question: how long to get initial quality numbers if we give you 5k de-identified notes?
01:35 Sofia (Redwood SE): typical flow: we take the dataset, build golden prompts and expected outputs, run a bench of ~1k to validate prompts, then scale to full 5k for quality eval. with our infra we can run the initial bench in 2-3 days once dataset is in our staging bucket. full run depends on throughput target — if you want 100 qps equivalent, we'll need dedicated pools configured.
01:51 Carlos: what about metrics beyond F1/EM? like hallucination rate, formatting errors, and a calibration score?
02:00 Sofia: good point. propose these metrics: 1) Exact Match (EM) for critical spans; 2) Token-level F1 for entity extraction; 3) Hallucination Rate — percent of responses containing unsupported facts (we detect via grounding checks against provided clinical labels and heuristics); 4) Format Error Rate — percent failing JSON schema; 5) Response Latency p50/p95/p99. we'll produce a combined quality score: weighted sum (EM*0.5 + (1 - hallucination_rate)*0.3 + (1 - format_error_rate)*0.2) — weights are suggested and adjustable.
02:29 Dr. Maya: that weighted score looks reasonable. can we see a worked example?
02:34 Sofia: yes, we'll include a sample scoring spreadsheet. for hallucinations detection we'll run regex and also external grounding — e.g., check med names against your formulary. manual spot-checks for ambiguous cases.
02:47 Evan: about golden prompts — we'll ask your SMEs to agree on 20-30 golden prompts per primary template: discharge summary extraction, medication reconciliation, diagnosis codification. these become the regression suite. we also recommend ~200 additional prompts for broader coverage.
03:02 Carlos: golden prompts will be curated from your labeled cases; we can provide 30 high-confidence ones per template by next week.
03:09 Dr. Maya: for regression tests, we want nightly runs during pilot and a baseline snapshot at start to catch regressions after model updates. can you automate test runs?
03:18 Sofia: yes, Redwood Console supports scheduled runs and diffs against baseline. we can alert on regressions and produce per-prompt deltas. note: small transcription glitch — sometimes our console labels are shown as redwood-console in the logs, but that's fine.
03:33 Priya: on data handling: what's the ingestion method? we need VPC egress restrictions and KMS for keys.
03:40 Evan (Redwood): ingestion options: secure S3 with VPC endpoints, or a customer-hosted SFTP into our staging within a private VPC. KMS integration supported for Redwood Dedicated and Private; hosted can use customer-managed keys via our KMS integration. we'll detail this in the security pack.
03:56 Sanjay: sizing: our workload is roughly 50k notes per day, average 700 tokens per note for LLM input, but for pilot we'll do a representative 5k subset. what throughput should we test?
04:08 Sofia: for 50k/day and a 12-hour window that's ~70 qps sustained. for pilot bench we can test at 10 qps sustained and burst up to 50 qps to see autoscaling behavior. we'll define target p99 latency (e.g., <700 ms for generation-only endpoints) and tokens/sec throughput per GPU.
04:26 Carlos: cost is a concern — we want per-unit cost estimate. will the eval run include quantized models?
04:33 Evan: we can test with Redwood-verified open models at FP16 and quantized int8 variants; we'll report cost estimates per 1k tokens across configs. Redwood Optimize will also suggest quantization profiles per workload.
04:45 Dr. Maya: hallucination thresholds — zero tolerance for fabricated medication names, but for non-critical contextual text maybe 2% acceptable?
04:54 Sofia: agree. we'll mark "critical fields" (medication, dosage, allergies) as must-pass EM and zero hallucination tolerance; other narrative fields will have softer thresholds.
05:06 Evan: scoring approach recap: per-prompt metrics -> aggregate per-template -> weighted quality score. we'll output CSVs and a dashboard in Redwood Console. also export per-prompt diffs for regression triage.
05:19 Carlos: how do you detect hallucinations automatically? can you show false positives/negatives?
05:24 Sofia: automatic detection uses two layers: 1) exact grounding against provided labels/formulary (fast, low FP), 2) heuristic semantic checks (NER + knowledge graph lookups) and a small ensemble model that flags likely hallucinations — those are then sampled for human review. we'll include manual spot-check rules to calibrate.
05:44 Priya: on compliance: we need audit logs and user access controls. RBAC?
05:49 Evan: Redwood supports RBAC, SAML SSO, and audit logs at request-level for Dedicated and Private. we'll include docs.
05:57 Dr. Maya: success criteria — here's what matters to us: EM >= 92% on critical spans, hallucination_rate < 0.5% for critical fields, format_error_rate < 1%, and p95 latency < 800ms. if we meet that on the 5k test set we consider pilot successful.
06:14 Evan: perfect, we'll codify that as the acceptance criteria in the eval plan.
06:20 Carlos: what about regression cadence — if you update models mid-pilot what happens?
06:24 Sofia: we recommend freezes on major model changes during evaluation windows or run A/B tests. Redwood can run parallel variants and compare. we'll set an automatic rollback policy if major regressions detected.
06:36 Sanjay: benchmark specifics — we want p50/p95/p99, throughput per GPU, cost per 1k tokens, and scaling behavior with batch size.
06:45 Sofia: yes, benchmark config we'll send includes: sequence length distribution, batch sizes, kernel/quantization configs, concurrency, and warm-up tokens. for KV cache and long context tests we'll include a 2-hour sustained run.
06:58 Dr. Maya: timeline — if we share dataset by 2026-08-06 can we have an initial report by 2026-08-13?
07:05 Evan: yes: security pack by 2026-08-06, golden prompts and eval dataset by 2026-08-07, SE runs initial bench 8/10-8/12, full 5k run and report by 8/13, follow-up review 8/20.
07:16 Carlos: ok. can you also include sample prompts for edge cases — redaction errors, shorthand notes?
07:22 Sofia: will do; we'll include negative tests to exercise hallucination triggers and formatting corner cases.
07:29 Priya: one more — can you provide example regression test entries as JSON with expected outputs so we can vet them?
07:36 Evan: yes, we'll include the regression suite as JSON lines with input, expected output, and tags.
07:41 Dr. Maya: any limitations we should know? biases, out-of-vocab meds?
07:45 Sofia: we'll document known limitations: newer proprietary drug names may require whitelist updates; quantized models might slightly reduce EM for tricky spans — we'll include both FP16 and int8 results.
07:58 Evan: perfect. recap of next steps: Evan send eval dataset template + golden prompt template by 8/7; Sofia send benchmark config and runbook by 8/9; security docs by 8/6. schedule bench week of 8/10 and review 8/20.
08:15 Carlos: thanks everyone, we'll start preparing the sanitized samples.
08:20 Dr. Maya: thanks, looking forward.
08:25 Evan: thanks — meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker labels may be generic; minor transcription mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "k v cache").
